html:
The northeast of Somalia, where frankincense and myrrh trees grow in the mountains, has supplied these resins to Egypt, Arabia, Rome and India since ancient times.

A Greek merchants' guide of the 1st century, the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, lists ports on the Somali coast such as Mosylon and Opone, trading incense, cinnamon and slaves for cloth and tools. Many scholars place the land of Punt, where Egyptians sailed for incense, in the Horn of Africa. The trade joined the incense route of Arabia.

Somali families still harvest frankincense today, and the region is still among the world's main sources. The trade made the coast part of the Indian Ocean world centuries before the rise of Mogadishu.
sum: The northeast of Somalia, where frankincense and myrrh trees grow in the mountains, has supplied these resins to Egypt, Arabia, Rome and India since ancient times.
